chunks: There is no believer who is afflicted by a calamity in this world, then recites istirja' at the time of his calamity and remains patient when the calamity strikes him, except that Allah forgives for him his past sins, except the major sins for which Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has made the Fire obligatory. And whenever he remembers his calamity in what remains of his life, then recites istirja' at it and praises Allah, Mighty and Majestic, at it, Allah forgives for him every sin he committed between the first istirja' and the last istirja', except the major sins.

key_terms.الْكَبَائِرَ: major sins excluded from the forgiveness mentioned here
key_terms.فَيَسْتَرْجِعُ: he recites istirja', saying that one belongs to Allah and returns to Him
key_terms.مُؤْمِنٍ: a believer, one characterized by iman
key_terms.مُصِيبَةٍ: a calamity or affliction that befalls a person
key_terms.وَحَمِدَ اللَّهَ: and he praised Allah in response

ai.seo_question: How does reciting istirja' during calamity affect a believer's sins?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that when a believer faces calamity with sabr and istirja', Allah grants forgiveness for past sins other than the major sins. It also shows that remembering the calamity later with renewed istirja' and praise of Allah becomes a means of ongoing forgiveness.
